ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is a cross-sectional distribution diagram of the magnetic field of an energized solenoid with a relatively large pitch and elasticity. The dashed line is the central axis of the solenoid (coinciding with a certain magnetic field line). ab is an energized straight wire suspended by an insulating thin string and located directly above the solenoid; its current direction is from a to b. The current is very small and does not affect the magnetic field of the solenoid. Which of the following statements is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: An electron whose gravity is not counted is injected into the solenoid along the central axis; the electron will make uniform rectilinear motion.

The dashed line is the central axis of the solenoid (coinciding with a certain magnetic field line). ab is an energized straight wire suspended by an insulating thin string and located directly above the solenoid; its current direction is from a to b. The current is very small and does not affect the magnetic field of the solenoid. Which of the following statements is correct?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: An electron whose gravity is not counted is injected into the solenoid along the central axis; the electron will make uniform rectilinear motion.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the lower part of the figure is the magnetic-field cross section of the energized solenoid, and multiple closed magnetic field lines are drawn around the solenoid; inside the solenoid there is a horizontal central-axis position, and the stem states that this dashed line coincides with a certain magnetic field line. Directly above the solenoid is suspended a horizontal straight wire ab, and the wire is marked with the current direction from a to b. Reasoning: If an electron whose gravity is not counted is injected along the central axis of the solenoid, then the initial velocity direction of the electron is along the central axis. The stem states that the central axis coincides with a certain magnetic field line, so the electron velocity direction is collinear with the magnetic field direction at that point. The magnitude of the Lorentz force is F=|q|vB sinθ. When v and B are parallel or antiparallel, θ is 0 or π, sinθ=0, so the magnetic force is zero. Also, because gravity is not counted and there are no other acting forces, the resultant force on the electron is zero, and both the magnitude and direction of the velocity do not change. Therefore the electron will make uniform rectilinear motion.
